title: Choose the console's visual world
question: The roll assigned The Laboratory Notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Laboratory Notebook
options.lineage: the bound, numbered, signed lab notebook
options.thesis: The console as the dated, numbered record of an experiment that spends money: nothing is ever erased, an uncertain action is struck and annotated, and the record keeps its numbering.
options.viewport: A fine blue-gray grid grounds the page; every turn is a ruled, numbered row (Nº 0142) with time and state; the uncertain escrow entry is struck through and annotated, never removed; readiness, spend and tasks sit as margin panels; the dark theme is the same notebook kept at night on slate.
options.risk: Reads austere or academic if the grid and numbering become decoration instead of record-keeping.

raised.raise: State is encoded in form as well as hue: solid, dashed, struck and doubled marks, so state survives colorblindness and print.
One status-mark geometry holds from tag size to banner size; only the scale changes.
The entry under focus is the brightest thing on the page; routine entries recede by tint, never by blur or shadow.
The dark theme's attention marks use a restrained night-annotation hue that marks without flooding night vision.

options.label: The Departure Check
options.lineage: the aviation checklist and pre-flight card
options.thesis: Every screen answers like a checklist: readiness rows with big binary marks, warnings reserved for real danger, and every money change confirmed as a challenge and a response before it counts.
options.viewport: Readiness leads as the pre-flight panel with oversized OK and Problem marks; attention items are warning boxes with one action each; the timeline reads as completed check items; Freeze and spending changes confirm as spelled-out challenge/response; the dark theme is the same card stock under cockpit-night light.
options.risk: The checklist-derived ops console is where most runs in this category land; familiar and effective, rarely surprising.

options.label: The Gate Board
options.lineage: the airport departure board paired with the boarding pass
options.thesis: A live board of commitments: rows in a fixed tabular rhythm rerank and update in place without losing identity, a changed row holds its alert color until the operator acknowledges it, and settled items drop off the board.
options.viewport: The timeline is the board: dark matte panel, mono tabular columns (time, kind, detail, state); the uncertain escrow row holds a signal-yellow edge until Mark checked clears it from the attention board; spend and readiness read as pass segments; the world ships both themes natively, the dark board and the paper pass.
options.case: Wins both axes: its core behavior is the product's own (a change holds its alert until acknowledged, rows keep identity as they rerank) and every operator alive has read a departure board; it beats the notebook on audience identification and product clarity.
options.risk: Board chrome (flap-display nostalgia, fake scan blocks) is a costume; only the tabular rhythm and the held-alert behavior may ship.

options.label: The Lexicon Page
options.thesis: A reference page for a long record: guide words at the head name the span in view, a shoulder margin carries the apparatus, and color is quarantined inside one bordered plate.
options.viewport: Engraving-black text on cream; the header carries guide words naming the first and last turn in view; a shoulder margin holds tags and times so entries stay clean; the environment banner is the page's one bordered color plate; the dark theme is the same page by lamplight.
options.case: Holds product clarity: guide words and the shoulder genuinely serve a long timeline; loses audience identification, since a 19th-century dictionary is not this operator's daily world.
options.risk: Serif UI text taxes scanning, and the antique voice can read as costume the moment a table or form appears.

options.label: The Emission Rail
options.case: Loses both axes: spectrograms are a scientist's instrument, not an operator's world, and seven wavelength hues collide with the money-safety color language.
options.kept: State encoded in form as well as hue, never hue alone.

options.label: The Bitmap Specimen
options.case: Loses both axes: coarse bitmap display faces tax every label on a working screen, and the audience reads records, not type specimens.
options.kept: One status-mark geometry at every scale.

options.label: The Title-Card Wall
options.case: Loses both axes: poster tiles need artwork the marketplace never supplies, and tile-by-tile focus fights the at-a-glance record.
options.kept: Focus carried by light: the lit row wins, the rest recede.

options.label: The Star Atlas
options.lineage: the celestial chart under red flashlight
options.case: Loses both axes: a coordinate sky charts objects in space while the console charts commitments in time, and operators do not navigate by constellations.
options.kept: A restrained night-annotation hue for attention in the dark theme.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern ops dashboard, played straight: neutral ground, near-black text, one blue accent, standard cards and tables at Linear/Stripe craft, with a first-class dark mode.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement every operator expects: top bar, attention alert, timeline table, sidebar stat cards, executed at full craft in both themes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
